title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, and starvation prevention
author: Arjun Patel
description: Motivation: Continuous batching had observable unfairness and occasional starvation for low-CPU/low-priority request classes under high load. This PR tunes scheduler queueing behavior, adds starvation-prevention heuristics, tightens timeouts, and exposes a small set of knobs to make trade-offs explicit. Changesets are focused and backwards-compatible: default behavior improves tail latency and fairness without changing external API. Summary of changes (high-level): 1) Introduce per-class queue reservations and a soft-eviction policy so high-throughput classes cannot monopolize batch slots; 2) Add starvation detector that promotes oldest-waiting requests into reserved slots when latency thresholds are exceeded; 3) Tighten per-request pre-batch timeout and expose it as config (defaults preserved for safety); 4) Improve batch assembly logic to prefer diversity of classes in a batch when doing so reduces tail latency; 5) Metrics: add per-class queue length, wait-time histogram, promotion-count, and eviction-count; 6) Tests & benchmarks: new unit/integration tests and microbench harness showing improvements. Benchmarks: internal lab runs on r5-gpu cluster show 8-12% median latency improvement at p95 and ~20% reduction in max wait-time for low-priority classes on mixed workloads. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag with telemetry and automated rollback if error-rate or tail latency regressions are observed. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - ENG-3127 - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Benchmarks added - [x] Metrics and dashboards updated - [x] Feature-flag gated - [x] Reviewed and approved by runtime team. Related: builds on previous continuous-batcher fixes (see ENG-2980) and addresses customer-reported SLA skew (SUP-2042).

release_notes: Tuned continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queue fairness and prevent starvation. Adds configurable reservations, promotion heuristics, new metrics, and defaults that improve mixed-workload tail latency. Rollout gated by feature flag.
notes_on_benchmarks: Microbench on r5-gpu: mixed workload (50% high-throughput small reqs, 50% low-priority long-gen) shows median p95 latency down 8-12% and max wait-time for low-priority class down ~20%. No regression on single-class throughput tests.
manual_steps: To roll out: enable feature flag for 10% of pods, monitor promotion_count, eviction_count, request_error_rate, and p95 latency for each class. If regressions >10% in p95 or errors spike, rollback the flag.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps defaults conservative; operators can tune reservations and pre-batch timeout in config. The promotion path is designed to be idempotent and observable via new metrics.
changelog: Added queue reservation and promotion; tightened pre-batch timeout; added metrics and tests; updated docs and chart values.
safety_impact: feature-flagged; defaults unchanged for release branches
